title: M6 MacBook Pro: Everything we know about Apple’s next laptop
content:
Macworld





Apple is expected to launch a new 14-inch MacBook Pro with the standard M6 chip in October 2026. However, unlike previous generations, the M6 isn’t expected to be joined by more powerful M6 Pro and M6 Max versions.
Apple currently offers three processor options across the MacBook Pro range: the standard M5 in the entry-level 14-inch model, and the more powerful M5 Pro and M5 Max in the 14-inch and 16-inch models. The standard M6 is expected to replace the M5 almost exactly a year after its October 2025 launch.
According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple is preparing to announce the entry-level M6 MacBook Pro in late October, potentially ahead of its October 28 media event. The new model is expected to retain the existing design, with the faster processor providing the main upgrade.
The more substantial changes, including an OLED touchscreen and redesigned chassis, are reportedly reserved for premium MacBook Pro models that will continue to use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. Rather than introducing M6 Pro and M6 Max processors, Apple is reportedly fast-tracking the M7 generation, with M7 Pro and M7 Max models expected in fall 2027. For more on the redesigned models arriving this year, see our touchscreen MacBook Pro guide.
That creates an unusual buying decision: choose the standard M6 MacBook Pro, opt for one of the redesigned touchscreen models with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, or wait for the next generation of professional processors in 2027. Here’s what the latest reports suggest.


M6 MacBook Pro release date: When will it launch?
October 28, 2026 (confirmed media experience date)
On October 19, Apple announced a media event, dubbed “Pro and Tell” on October 28, 2026. This is expected to be the introduction of new Macs, including the M6 MacBook Pro.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported on October 8 that Apple is planning to announce the M6 MacBook Pro on October 27, 2026. According to the report, the launch will include an online video presentation and an in-person component for the press.
More recently, reports have pointed to a media experience in Los Angeles on Wednesday, October 28, a day after Gurman’s originally reported announcement date. Apple could still unveil the new MacBook Pro on October 27 before giving invited journalists an opportunity to see the hardware the following day. 
Then on Monday October 19, Apple’s Greg Joswiak posted on X to say: “Can’t wait to pro and tell next week.”  Indicating that the MacBook Pro will be updated in the week of 26 October.  


Can’t wait to pro and tell next week. pic.twitter.com/3wUkxwq35i
— Greg Joswiak (@gregjoz) October 19, 2026





The M6 MacBook Pro is expected to launch alongside the first OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro, an M6 iMac, and an updated iPad mini. The new entry-level MacBook Pro is expected to retain its 14-inch display and existing design, with the M6 chip providing the main upgrade.
The late October announcement would fit Apple’s recent release pattern. The M5 MacBook Pro arrived in October 2025, while its predecessor launched in November 2024.
Of the five generations of MacBook Pro, five have been released in the October/November timeframe. The list below also demonstrates that Apple doesn’t always introduce the standard, Pro and Max versions of a chip generation together.  
M5 Pro & M5 Max MacBook Pro: March 2026
M5 MacBook Pro: October 2025
M4, M4 Pro & M4 Max MacBook Pro: November 2024
M3, M3 Pro & M3 Max MacBook Pro: November 2023
M2 Pro & M2 Max MacBook Pro: January 2023
M2 MacBook Pro: June 2022
M1 Pro & M1 Max MacBook Pro: October 2021
M1 MacBook Pro: November 2020
Following the October 27 or 28 announcement, Gurman has indicated that the new MacBook Pro will start shipping on November 6. Ongoing memory and storage chip shortages could still affect availability or delivery times. These supply constraints have already contributed to price increases across Apple’s Mac lineup.


						

							


M6 MacBook Pro: Chip details
Expected M6 specs:
Same 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU as in the existing M6 Mac mini
TSMC 2nm manufacturing process
Up to 170GB/s memory bandwidth
Improved AI processing with Neural Accelerators

				
					

				
			
The M6 chip is expected to incorporate new features for improved AI processing.

Apple




Apple has introduced the M6 chip in the Mac mini, giving us a clear idea of what to expect from the upcoming MacBook Pro. The M6 is Apple’s first M-series chip built using TSMC’s 2nm manufacturing process, bringing improvements to CPU, GPU, and AI performance.
The M6 in the Mac mini features a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, up from the M5’s 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU. It also introduces Neural Accelerators in every GPU core and a dual 16-core Neural Engine, boosting performance in AI workloads. The M6 MacBook Pro is expected to benefit from the same architectural improvements, making it particularly appealing to users running AI-powered applications and local AI models.
The Mac mini also provides an indication of what to expect from memory bandwidth. Earlier rumors suggested the M6 could reach 200GB/s, but the M6 Mac mini delivers up to 170GB/s with 24GB or 32GB of unified memory. The 16GB configuration offers 153GB/s, matching the M5. This relatively modest increase could limit the performance gains delivered by the redesigned GPU.
Our analysis suggests that the additional GPU cores, higher clock speeds, and architectural improvements help the M6 deliver gains of 20 percent or more in 3D graphics performance. However, memory bandwidth limitations mean those gains aren’t as substantial as the additional processing power might suggest.
The MacBook Pro’s exact M6 specifications remain unconfirmed, but the Mac mini offers a useful preview of the chip’s capabilities. The key question is whether Apple will make further changes to the processor or memory configurations when it brings the M6 to the MacBook Pro.


						

							


M6 MacBook Pro: Other specifications and features
Existing 14-inch design expected; no OLED or touchscreen
The M6 MacBook Pro is expected to retain the existing 14-inch design, with few changes beyond the processor upgrade. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the display, chassis, and other hardware are likely to remain substantially unchanged from the M5 MacBook Pro.
That means buyers shouldn’t expect an OLED display or touchscreen on the standard M6 model. Those features are reportedly reserved for Apple’s redesigned premium MacBook Pro models, which are also expected to debut on October 27.

				
					

				
			
The M6 MacBook Pro could be the last entry-level model of this particular design.

Foundry




How is the M6 MacBook Pro different from the touchscreen MacBook Pro?
Apple is reportedly preparing two very different MacBook Pro updates for October 27.
The standard 14-inch MacBook Pro will move from the M5 to the M6 processor while retaining its familiar design. It should appeal to buyers who want the newer chip but don’t need a redesigned laptop.
The higher-end MacBook Pro models, meanwhile, are expected to introduce an OLED touchscreen, a reportedly thinner and lighter chassis, and potentially an iPhone-style Dynamic Island camera cutout. Despite these upgrades, the redesigned models will reportedly use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips rather than M6 Pro and M6 Max processors.
This reflects Apple’s reported decision to skip the M6 Pro and M6 Max generation and focus development resources on the M7 family, which is expected in 2027.
Although the standard M6 is a newer chip, the M5 Pro and M5 Max are designed for more demanding professional workloads, so buyers shouldn’t assume the M6 MacBook Pro will be the more powerful option. It’s a similar situation to the Mac mini lineup, where the standard model features the M6 chip while the higher-end configuration uses the M5 Pro. 
The choice could therefore come down to whether buyers prioritize the latest chip at a lower price or a more powerful MacBook Pro with a redesigned display and chassis.


						

							






FeatureM6 MacBook ProOLED touchscreen MacBook Pro

Expected announcementOctober 27, 2026October 27, 2026
ProcessorM6M5 Pro / M5 Max
Screen sizes14-inchPremium MacBook Pro sizes; expected 14- and 16-inch
DisplayExisting non-OLED displayOLED
TouchscreenNoYes
DesignExisting chassisThinner, lighter redesign
PriceFrom around $1,999Higher pricing expected

 






M6 MacBook Pro: Price
$1,999/£1,999 starting price possible
We haven’t heard any reports about the price of the entry-level M6 MacBook Pro, but we can look at recent price history to get an idea. When the M5 MacBook Pro was released in 2025, its starting price was $1,599. Apple bumped it to $1,699 when the M5 Pro and Max models arrived earlier this year and increased the starting storage to 1TB. This past June, however, Apple raised the price to $1,999 due to supply chain constraints. Those constraints aren’t going away anytime soon, and it’s likely that the higher price is now the new normal.
During Apple’s Q3 2026 financial announcement in July, Apple CEO Tim Cook and CFO Kevan Parekh made it a point to explain that the supply chain constraints will affect production costs for months to come. ” We expect the impact from supply constraints to increase significantly sequentially,” said Parekh. “The projected supply constraints in the September quarter affect iPhone, Mac, and iPad.” Cook said, “With less flexibility in supply chain, we expect the impact from the supply constraints to increase significantly sequentially.”
The existing M5 MacBook Pro starts at $1,999/£1,999, following the price increases introduced in June 2026, and the M6 could retain that starting price.
However, another price increase is possible. Ongoing memory and storage shortages continue to affect Apple’s manufacturing costs, and the company may need to pass some of those costs on to buyers.
The redesigned OLED touchscreen models are also expected to carry a premium over the existing MacBook Pro lineup, making the standard M6 a potentially more affordable alternative for buyers who want a new MacBook Pro without paying extra for the redesigned display and chassis.


						

							


Should you wait for the M6 MacBook Pro?
With Apple’s next MacBook Pro announcement reportedly just days away, there’s a strong argument for waiting before buying a new 14-inch MacBook Pro. 
Waiting until the end of October should provide a clearer picture of the M6 MacBook Pro’s performance, pricing, and availability, while potentially bringing discounts on the outgoing M5 model.
Wait for the M6 MacBook Pro if: You’re planning to buy the standard 14-inch MacBook Pro and don’t urgently need a new laptop. The M6 should provide improved CPU, GPU, and AI performance over the M5, without requiring a move to Apple’s more expensive Pro and Max models.
Consider the OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro if: You’re interested in a more substantial upgrade, particularly the rumored touchscreen display, OLED technology, and thinner design. Those models are expected to continue using M5 Pro and M5 Max processors, making them potentially better choices for demanding professional workloads.
Buy an M5 MacBook Pro now if: You need a laptop immediately or find a substantial discount. The existing M5, M5 Pro, and M5 Max MacBook Pro models remain capable machines, and a reduced price could make them better value than a newly launched M6 model.
Wait for the M7 MacBook Pro if: You’re particularly interested in OLED but don’t need the touchscreen. Reports suggest Apple’s entry-level MacBook Pro could adopt the redesigned OLED chassis in 2027 with an M7 processor, although the timing remains uncertain.
For most people considering the entry-level MacBook Pro, waiting until October 27 makes sense. Even if the M6 doesn’t offer enough of an improvement to justify its price, its arrival could create opportunities to buy the outgoing M5 model at a discount.

title: Next Apple event 2026: When is Apple’s next launch?
content:
Macworld





Apple announced HomeView, HomePod mini 2, a new Apple TV 4K and the Apple Home Collection at its “Welcome Home” launch on October 13, 2026. But that will not be its final announcements this month.
Apple has now indicated that new products are coming next week. On Monday October 19, Apple’s Greg Joswiak posted on X to say: “Can’t wait to pro and tell next week.” 
This follows news that Apple has invited selected media to another product launch experience, this time in Los Angeles on Wednesday October 28. That new date is a day after the date reported by Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, who initially reported that another launch was planned for October 27. The product launch could still take place on the 27 October though.
Apple is expected to reveal a touchscreen MacBooks, an M6 14-inch MacBook Pro, an M6 iMac and an OLED iPad mini and these are likely to be the products being showcased at the media event. 
Apple typically has four main event windows each year: a spring event, WWDC in June, the iPhone event in September, and sometimes a further event in October. The company rarely confirms dates far in advance, and there’s no guarantee it will hold an event in every window. That leaves Apple fans – and anyone considering a new Apple device – wondering when the next event will happen and what might be announced. Fortunately, Apple’s annual schedule is fairly predictable, while reliable rumours often provide additional clues about what’s coming. That means we can make informed estimates about the timing of future keynotes and the products most likely to appear.Here’s everything we know about the next event Apple will hold – and beyond.


When is Apple’s next event?
October 28, 2026: Apple’s confirmed ‘Pro and Tell’ media experience in Los Angeles.
Apple has invited some media to a product launch experience on October 28 in Los Angeles. The event starts at 10 a.m. Pacific / 1 p.m. Eastern / 5 p.m. U.K. (clocks change on October 25 in the U.K.) 
The next launch may still take place on October 27, 2026, the date initially reported by Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman.
Gurman previously said the launch will include a video presentation and a gathering for journalists. Apple held a “Welcome Home” experience for select media on October 13. In March, it also hosted an “Apple Experience” alongside three days of product announcements. Those launches suggest a possible model for late October.


						

							


What could Apple launch at the next event?
Apple is expected to unveil its long-rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro, a 14-inch MacBook Pro with an M6 chip, an M6 iMac and an OLED iPad mini at the reported October 27 or 28 launch.
Joswiak’s X post indicates that the MacBook Pro will be the headliner for the event: 


Can’t wait to pro and tell next week. pic.twitter.com/3wUkxwq35i
— Greg Joswiak (@gregjoz) October 19, 2026

Apple has held four events so far in 2026, including its March and October hands-on Experiences. On March 4, the company invited select media to hands-on “experiences” in multiple locations. In the run-up to that date, Apple launched several products via press release, including the iPhone 17e, M4 iPad Air, and M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pro, M5 MacBook Air and the MacBook Neo.
The second event was WWDC, which began with a keynote on June 8. At the WWDC keynote Apple outlined the upcoming changes to its operating systems, including iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate.
In August Apple issued press releases to announce the new Mac mini and Mac Studio. 
At the September 9 event Apple unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, a foldable iPhone Duo, a new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and AirPods 5. 
Apple’s October 13 “Welcome Home” announcements included HomeView, a new smart-home display with a 7-inch touchscreen; HomePod mini 2; a fourth-generation Apple TV 4K with an updated Siri Remote; and the Apple Home Collection, a range of cameras, doorbells, locks, and thermostats developed with accessory partners.  

				
					

				
			
Calendars at the ready.

Foundry





 FAQ 


1.
How far in advance does Apple announce an event?
Apple usually announces its events around one to two weeks before they take place, although the timing varies. The October 13, 2026 Experience was announced just five days in advance. Apple also sometimes chooses to announce products via press release without holding an event. 





2.
What time will the next Apple Event start? 
The Pro and Tell media experience in Los Angeles will start at 10 a.m. Pacific. That’s 1 p.m. Eastern and 5 p.m. U.K. (the U.K. clocks change before this event.)
This won’t be a keynote in the traditional sense. 
Apple keynotes usually last between one and two hours and feature the CEO alongside various other Apple executives.
WWDC and the September event tend to be longer keynotes; the spring and late-fall events can be slightly shorter. 
For example, the September 2024 event was 1 hour 38 minutes.





3.
What time do Apple events normally start in U.S., U.K. and other global time zones?
Apple’s events tend to start at 10 am PT or 1 pm ET. That translates to the following times in the countries where most of our readers live:
U.S.: 10 am PDT, 11 am MDT, 12 pm CDT, 1 pm EDT
Canada: as above, plus 2 pm ADT
U.K.: 6 pm
Europe: 7 pm CEST, 8 pm EEST
India: 10:30 pm IST
Australia: next day — 1 am AWST, 2:30 am ACST, 3 am AEST
New Zealand: next day — 5 am NZST
The timings are generally the same for all Apple Keynotes, but can be slightly different if Apple holds the event during the period of a couple of weeks when the clocks have changed in the U.S. but not elsewhere (in 2026 the clocks will change in the U.S. on November 1, while in the U.K. they change on October 25).
Sometimes Apple holds events at different times, for example, in October 2023 the event was held in late afternoon in San Francisco, which meant it was midnight in the U.K. The event on October 13, 2026 started at 9 am in New York, 2 pm in the U.K.
If Apple doesn’t hold an event and instead just issues a press release, that usually happens around 8 am PT, 11 am ET and 4 pm U.K. time.





4.
How often does Apple hold events?
There can be as many as four Apple events in a year:  
Spring Event
WWDC in June
iPhone Event in September
Late Fall Event in October
This event calendar is by no means set in stone, though, with the spring and October events being less regular. Some years, Apple doesn’t hold a spring event at all. In 2025 Apple only held two events, preferring instead to announce new products via press release.





5.
Will there be a live stream at the next Apple Event?
There was no public livestream for the October 13 Experience and one isn’t expected for the rumored October 27 or 28 event.
Apple usually livestreams the iPhone announcement in September and the WWDC keynote in June. 





6.
Does Apple ever announce products without an event? 
Apple frequently announces products without a keynote event, often opting for press releases or multi-day announcement windows. In recent years, the company has increasingly reserved its large-scale media events for major flagship launches, such as the primary iPhone lineup in September, while using press releases for iterative updates or “chip bumps” that may not warrant a full hour-long presentation.





7.
How to watch an Apple event
Apple events are typically broadcast across several digital platforms, allowing viewers to tune in from almost any device. While the company previously restricted access to its own hardware or the Safari browser, these barriers have been removed in recent years.
You can access live Apple presentations through the following official channels:
YouTube: This is often considered the easiest way to watch. Apple streams its keynotes live on its official YouTube channel, which can be accessed via any web browser or the YouTube app on smartphones, tablets, and smart TVs.
Apple.com: The company hosts a dedicated “Events” page on its official website. For the best experience on a PC, it is recommended to use Microsoft Edge on Windows 10 or later.
Apple TV App: The stream is available within the Apple TV app on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple TV hardware. Keynotes are usually listed in the app’s lineup a day or two before the event begins.
Apple Podcasts: Apple also showcases its events through the Podcasts app on Apple devices, where you can watch the video presentation.
We usually run a Live Blog which will provide minute-by-minute text updates and analysis as products are announced.
Following the end of the event, detailed breakdowns will also be available on the Macworld Podcast, which can be found on Spotify, Soundcloud, and Apple Podcasts. 








Will Apple have a second October event in 2026?

				
					

				
			
Apple




Apple has already unveiled new products on October 13 at an ‘Apple Experience’ in New York, but it seems there are more product launches in the pipeline.
A separate Mac and iPad launch is reportedly planned for October 27 or 28. A touchscreen MacBook, M6 14-inch MacBook Pro, M6 iMac and OLED iPad mini are rumored.


						

							


Will Apple hold a spring event in 2027? 

				
					

				
			John Ternus: Apple’s new CEO.
Michael Simon / Foundry




Apple’s spring events have become increasingly unpredictable. The company has not held a traditional spring event since May 2024, although it did invite members of the media, including Macworld, to a “Special Apple Experience” in 2026. 
Rather than a keynote presentation, the March 4, 2026 gathering was a hands-on showcase that followed three days of product announcements, including the MacBook Neo, iPhone 17e, and M5 MacBook Air.
Will Apple take a similar approach to spring product launches in 2027? It’s certainly possible. The format appeared to work well, allowing each product announcement to receive its own media coverage rather than competing for attention during a single event. 
Apple is expected to release three iPhone models in spring 2027 – or it could be two new iPhones, with the Air and iPhone 18 merging.
iPhone 18 (base model)
iPhone 18e
iPhone Air 2
Apple may also update the MacBook Air with an M6 processor in spring 2027. 


						

							


When is WWDC 2027?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




When is the WWDC keynote?
In 2026 the WWDC keynote was on Monday June 8. In 2025 it started on Monday June 9. We expect WWDC will start on Monday 7 June in 2027. 
WWDC generally runs from the Monday to Friday in the second week of June. 
What Apple could launch at WWDC
WWDC is Apple’s big developer event at which it reveals plans for the operating systems that run on Apple hardware.
In June 2027 we expect Apple to unveil details of iOS 28, iPadOS 28, macOS 28, updates to watchOS, tvOS, HomePod software, and an update to Apple’s realityOS.
Apple sometimes announces new hardware at WWDC, usually the high-end models targeted at power users, so we could see new Macs.
Following the keynote on Monday, developer events and sessions will run throughout the week. You can read more about WWDC date, times and everything you need to know in a separate article.


						

							


What did Apple launch at past events?
So far in 2026 Apple has held an ‘experience’, which rather than being an event in the traditional sense, was a chance for journalists to get a look at products Apple had launched in the days prior, including MacBook Neo and iPhone 17e. The company also hosted the WWDC keynote on June 8, at which it revealed its plans for Apple Intelligence and Siri in iOS 27, macOS 27 and the other operating systems. Apple held its iPhone launch event on September 9 at which the iPhone 18 Pro and Max, iPhone Duo, Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and AirPods 5 launched. Plus Apple has unveiled new Home focused products (HomeView, HomePod mini 2 and Apple TV 4K) at a “Welcome Home” experience on October 13. 
In 2025 Apple only held two events. The first was its Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) on June 9, at which it introduced the new features coming in the next version of its operating systems, and the second was the huge September 9 Apple Event where it launched new Apple Watches, new AirPods Pro and the new iPhones for 2025.
Apple doesn’t have to hold an event to launch new products though. Prior to WWDC, Apple launched a new iPhone 16e via press release on February 19, a new iPad and iPad Air via press release on March 4, and a new MacBook Air and Mac Studio on March 5. 
Apple then went on to launch a new M5 MacBook Pro and M5 iPad Pro in October. No event was held to mark these launches.
In 2024, Apple held three events: one on Tuesday, May 7, at which it launched new iPads; a keynote to kick off WWDC on June 10; and an event on September 9 at which Apple unveiled the new iPhone 16, Apple Watch Series 10 and the AirPods 4. In October 2024 there was no event, but Apple did announce new products (iMac, Mac mini and MacBook Pro) via press release.
In 2023 there were three events: WWDC in June, an iPhone event in September, and Apple’s second fall event on October 30 (or after midnight on October 31 if you weren’t in the U.S.).
In 2022 Apple held three events: a spring event on March 8, WWDC on June 6, and the iPhone 14 launch on September 7. In other years Apple has held four events though.

title: This MacBook Pro isn’t just cheap, it’s $400 less than Apple’s pre-surge price
content:
Macworld





		
Apple MacBook Pro M5 Max
View Deal
If you want the best laptop you can possibly get, you’d better be prepared to spend quite a bit of money. The RAM and storage crisis has forced Apple and the rest of the industry to raise prices on just about everything, with the highest-end laptops getting the biggest increases. For example, the top-of-the-line 16-inch M5 Max MacBook Pro with 36GB of RAM and 2TB of storage jumped $500, from $3,899 to $4,399, and we haven’t seen it dip much below $4,000 since. 
Until now. Amazon is selling this MacBook Pro for $3,499, a whopping savings of $900 off its current MSRP and $400 under the price it was before the Great Summer Price Hike. That’s not just a great deal; it’s the lowest price we’ve ever seen, before or after the price hike.
The best part is that this is really a pro-level laptop that can handle all your projects, whether you’re editing video or working on AI models. The device runs on the M5 Max chip with an 18-core CPU and a 32-core GPU that will make video edits and 3D work run as smoothly as butter. Each GPU core has a Neural Accelerator, so AI tools run right on the laptop too. With 36GB of unified memory, you can keep dozens of apps and tabs open without issue. The 2TB SSD holds plenty of files, too, and you’re unlikely to need an upgrade anytime soon.
The spacious 16.2-inch Liquid Retina XDR display is stunning, hitting 1600 nits peak brightness with an impressive contrast ratio. There are three Thunderbolt 5 ports that can handle fast drives and up to four external displays. You also get HDMI, an SD card slot, MagSafe charging, and Wi-Fi 7. In short, you won’t have to worry about upgrading for years.
So go grab it for $3,499 while it’s still $900 off because this deal won’t last forever. And we doubt it’ll go much lower, even with Black Friday around the corner.

title: GM Says Apple Wallet Car Keys Coming to These Vehicles
content:
In a late September press release that we just discovered now, GM announced that it has started rolling out Apple Wallet car key support in select Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC vehicle models, with additional models to follow over time.


Google Wallet and Samsung Wallet will also be supported, with a related Samsung press release mentioning availability in the U.S. and Canada.

GM said the rollout will occur as follows, with model years listed in parentheses.

September–October 2026


  
Cadillac Vistiq (2027)

  
Cadillac Optiq (2026–2027)

  
Cadillac Lyriq (2025–2027)



December 2026


  
Cadillac Escalade (2027)

  
Cadillac Escalade IQ/IQL (2027)

  
Chevrolet Suburban (2026–2027)

  
Chevrolet Tahoe (2026–2027)

  
GMC Yukon (2026–2027)

  
GMC Yukon XL (2026–2027)

GM said customers will see a notification in the "What's New" section of their vehicle's mobile app when digital key support is available.

Apple Wallet's car key feature allows you to use a compatible iPhone or Apple Watch as a vehicle's car key. GM said supported vehicles will automatically unlock as you approach and lock when you walk away. You can also open the vehicle's trunk and turn the climate control system on or off right from the Apple Wallet app.


GM's digital keys use ultra-wideband technology to enable secure, proximity-based authentication, along with Bluetooth. They work with the iPhone 11 or later (excluding iPhone SE 2, iPhone SE 3, and iPhone 16e) or an Apple Watch Series 6 or later.

HomeView will probably sell just fine, partly because it’s a comparatively affordable $299 and partly because it has the excitement and cachet of a brand-new Apple product. But that doesn’t mean it’s flawless. After all, HomeView is a first-gen device, and such devices nearly always suffer from problems that will be addressed in later versions.
In the latest edition of his Power On newsletter, Bloomberg leaker Mark Gurman draws attention to what he thinks is an obvious shortcoming of the HomeView: its inability to turn its screen to face the user. “In one commercial,” he writes, “a family passes the unit around… Each person has to physically turn the screen toward themselves. It’s an awkward demonstration for a device that’s supposed to make interacting with technology in the home more seamless.” This unwitting demonstration of a failing with the product, Gurman argues, “practically screams for a display that can turn on its own.”
Fortunately Gurman has good news for anyone who is similarly disenchanted by the lack of an auto-swivelling screen on the first-gen HomeView. The next version of the product, he claims, will feature a motorised robotic arm which will enable the screen to turn through 360 degrees and (based on voice recognition software) automatically face whoever is talking to it. “Imagine a FaceTime call where the screen follows you as you move around the kitchen,” he explains, “or a family gathered around a countertop with the display automatically turning toward whoever is speaking.”
The new model, Gurman stresses, is not just a sequel: it’s an upgrade. Aside from the robotic arm it will also boast a larger screen, up from 7 inches to 9. It probably won’t just be called HomeView, with likely branding options including a Max or Ultra suffix.
This isn’t the first time we’ve heard about a robotic smart device. Last year, Apple published a paper describing research into the technology (with videos), and we’ve read rumors about such a device for years.
Gurman claims this version of HomeView is already in development and carries the codename J595. (The original HomeView is J490.) It’s planned for release in 2027 or 2028, he adds. That’s quite a large window, but the development cycle for the original device lasted so long, he says, that long-departed Apple employees popped up after its launch to boast of involvement in its creation. Hopefully we won’t have to wait quite so long this time around.
creator: Macworld

title: Apple Photos faceprint privacy lawsuit pared down a bit, will continue
content:
A $32.5 billion class-action lawsuit involving the Illinois Biometric Privacy Act and iPhone Photos has been pared down, with the judge partially granting an Apple motion for summary judgment and decertifying one subclass.


Photos' facial features are at the heart of a privacy lawsuit
In August, a lawsuit surfaced alleging that Apple violated the Illinois Biometric Privacy Act (BIPA). It was claimed that Apple collected biometric data without user consent, via the Photos app.
However, in a September 30 filing by U.S. District Judge Nancy Rosenstengel, the class-action fight has been severely cut back. In a 34-page filing, the judge partially agrees with an Apple motion, while decertifying one of the subclasses in the suit.

title: AI audio firm Samplab acquired by Apple to boost Logic Pro
content:
Apple has acquired AI audio editing firm Samplab, likely to extend Logic Pro's existing stem splitting tools, as well as adding the ability to edit individual notes in chords.


Samplab was a stem-splitting music editor - image credit: Samplab.
Following its deal with the Huxe AI podcast company, Apple has now acquired Zurich-based Samplab under a similar arrangement. As detailed in the European Union's public list of acquisitions, Apple is to acquire certain assets, and offer employment to certain Samplab employees.
Samplab was founded in Hauptsitz, Zurich, Switzerland, in 2020 by Manuel Fritsche and Gian-Marco Hutter. It's believed to have no more than 10 employees and based on LinkedIn profiles, may even only employ the two founders.
